chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:

I said to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'May Allah make you succeed! People narrate that as-Sufyani will rise after the rule of the Banu al-Abbas has declined.' He said: 'They tell falsehood! As-Sufyani will rise while their rule is still prevailing.'

key_terms.أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ: A respectful address meaning 'May Allah rectify/improve you' or 'May Allah make you succeed'
key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيَّ: As-Sufyani, a key eschatological figure in Shia tradition who rises before the appearance of Imam al-Mahdi

ai.seo_question: When does as-Sufyani rise in relation to the Abbasid Caliphate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) corrects the common eschatological assumption that the rise of as-Sufyani marks the immediate end of Abbasid rule, clarifying instead that he emerges while their political authority still stands. This distinction highlights a period of overlapping or transitional authority, a key nuance in Shia hadith literature regarding the pre-Mahdi geopolitical landscape.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (11) Ali bin Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from Muhammad bin Musa from Ahmad bin Abu Ahmad from Muhammad bin Ali al-Qarashi that al-Hasan bin al-Jahm had said:

“Once I said to Imam ar-Redha (as): “May Allah make you succeed! People narrate that as-Sufyani will rise after the rule of the Abbasids declines.” He said: “They tell but falseness! As-Sufyani will rise while the rule of the Abbasids is still prevailing.”
